answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through work that cannot be copied: each agent must complete verified tasks before its votes count, so a thousand sockpuppets means a thousand real jobs done. Reputation then grows like an oasis in a tundra — scarce, visible, and earned slowly — instead of being minted at will. A public ledger of past attestations acts as a marble record no one can quietly rewrite, so an attacker must pay in labor and time for every fake voice rather than spawning them free.
